biography: Henrik Roos, a name whispered with a mix of admiration and exasperation in racing paddocks, hails from a small village in southern Sweden, a place more accustomed to the gentle hum of Volvo engines than the roar of a Dodge Viper GTS. His entry into motorsport was almost accidental; a local ice racing event, a borrowed Volvo 240, and an unexpected victory against seasoned veterans ignited a passion that quickly consumed him. Roos rapidly climbed the ranks, his raw talent undeniable, but his temperament often proving to be his undoing. A defining moment came at the Spa 24 Hours, where, leading comfortably in the final hour, a moment of overconfidence led to a costly crash, handing the victory to a rival. Now, at 26, Roos is considered to be at his peak, showcasing exceptional speed and race craft at times, yet still prone to the occasional lapse in judgement, leaving many to wonder if he'll ever truly harness his potential. He's currently making waves in the GT circuit, and many believe his inconsistency makes him more exciting to watch.
drivingStyle: Roos possesses an aggressive, attacking driving style, often bordering on reckless. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to push the car to its absolute limit, frequently flirting with the edge of control. While this approach yields spectacular results on occasion, it also contributes to his inconsistency. Tire management is a known weakness, as he tends to overdrive the car early in a stint, sacrificing long-term pace for immediate gains. Under pressure, Roos can either elevate his performance or completely unravel, depending on the day. He thrives on the adrenaline of a close battle, often relishing wheel-to-wheel combat, but can become frustrated and prone to errors if he feels unfairly challenged or disadvantaged.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial overtaking maneuver that cost Bellini a championship victory; the two have exchanged heated words and aggressive moves on track ever since.
Roos and Petrova have a rivalry rooted in their contrasting driving styles – Roos' aggressive approach clashes with Petrova's clinical precision, leading to frequent on-track clashes.
Tanaka and Roos have a rivalry mostly off the track. The two constantly try to goad each other into mistakes, and whoever wins the psychological battle tends to win the race.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, despite their increasingly questionable condition.
Listens to Swedish death metal at ear-splitting volume immediately before every race.
Has a peculiar habit of meticulously cleaning his helmet visor with a specific brand of microfiber cloth, regardless of its actual cleanliness.
famousQuote: "If you're not on the edge, you're taking up too much space."
careerHighlight: Winning the GT World Championship race at Monza in 2022, after starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical issue in qualifying, showcasing his ability to fight through the field and deliver a stunning victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Spa 24 Hours in the final hour, costing his team a certain victory and earning him considerable criticism for his impetuous driving.
